_readme: EXAMPLE engagement-api deployment config. Every identifier below is a
placeholder. Fill it from scripts/engagement-api-infra-discover.sh output —
never by hand and never by guessing.
Usage:
ENGAGEMENT_API_INFRA_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/your-config.json
DO NOT COMMIT a filled copy containing live identifiers. Only this example
and infra/cdk/fixtures/engagement-api.test.json belong in the repository.
Fields the plan fixes and validation rejects if changed:
cpu 512, memoryMiB 1024, desiredCount 1, minimumCount 1, maximumCount 2,
previewRulePriority 6, imageRepositoryName capiro/<environment>/engagement-api,
allowPublicIp false, allowEcsExec false.
Database budget must satisfy both:
observedSevenDayPeak + maximumCount * perTaskPoolMaximum <= floor(max * 0.80)
databaseMaxConnections - projectedPeak >= databaseMaxConnections * 0.10
If Phase 1 hardcodes a pool maximum that breaks this, stop and remediate
Phase 1. Do not raise Aurora capacity in Phase 2.
databaseMaxConnections: on Aurora Serverless v2, max_connections is the
formula LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392, 5000), not a fixed number —
it scales with current ACU. Live discovery (2.15, capiro-dev, 2026-08-06)
found capiro-dev-data's cluster at 0.5-16 ACU. Budget against the FLOOR
(MinCapacity), never the currently-scaled value — do not guess a single
number without checking the current ACU range via
aws rds describe-db-clusters --query DBClusters[0].ServerlessV2ScalingConfiguration.
databaseHostSecretArn and databaseAppSecretArn are DIFFERENT secrets. Live
discovery found the main API's own task splits DB credentials the same
way: /capiro/<env>/aurora/master supplies host/port,
/capiro/<env>/aurora/app supplies username/password. databaseName is not
a secret at all on that task — it is a literal env var (e.g. "capiro").
uiContract pins the accepted Phase 2.1 and 2.2 contracts. Recompute with:

node -e "const{createHash}=require('crypto'),fs=require('fs');const d='apps/api/src/engagement/__fixtures__/';const h=f=>createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(d+f)).digest('hex');console.log(h('outreach-v3-prototype-state-manifest.v1.json'),h('outreach-v3-ui-api-capability-manifest.v1.json'))"
These are nonsecret provenance values. They do not enable any UI.
clerkJwtIssuer is REQUIRED. engagement-api runs the identical NestJS
ConfigModule validator as the main API, which fatally refuses to boot
without it outside NODE_ENV=test. Use the SAME value the live
environment's other services already use (see lib/config.ts's
clerkJwtIssuer for dev/staging/prod) — do not invent a new Clerk
instance for this service.
